cards.text: Jacob, also called Israel, calls all his sons together and tells them to gather around and listen to their father. He's about to tell them what will happen to them in the days to come. Friend, when your father says "Gather around," you put the cookie DOWN.

cards.question: Jacob starts with his firstborn son, the oldest of them all. That's ___.

cards.text: Jacob calls Reuben his might and the beginning of his strength, excelling in honor, excelling in power. That's a review I'd FRAME and hang over my oven, but hold on to your apron, friend.

cards.question: After all that praise, Jacob says Reuben will keep on excelling.
Jacob tells Reuben he will no longer excel. What reason does Jacob give?

cards.text: Next, Jacob takes two sons at once, Simeon and Levi, and says their swords are weapons of violence. Friend, when Dad lumps you in with your brother, it is NEVER for a gold star.

cards.question: Jacob says he hopes to join Simeon and Levi's council.
Jacob wants to stay out of Simeon and Levi's assembly. What reason does he give?

answers.text: They kill men in their anger
They refused to come to Egypt

cards.text: Then Jacob says, “Cursed be their anger, for it is strong, and their wrath, for it is cruel!” Look close, friend: it's the anger and the wrath he curses.

cards.question: Because of their anger, Jacob says he will ___ Simeon and Levi in Israel.

cards.text: Three sons in and it's been ROUGH, so if I'm next, I'm sliding behind my mustache real slow. Then Jacob turns to Judah.

cards.question: Judah's turn sounds very different from his older brothers'. What does Jacob say Judah's brothers will do?

answers.text: Praise him and bow down to him
Turn on him and drive him out
Forget him and leave him behind

cards.text: Jacob says Judah is a young lion, coming back from the prey. “Like a lion he crouches and lies down; like a lioness, who dares to rouse him?”

cards.question: Jacob's lion picture makes Judah sound weak and easy to push around.

cards.text: Then Jacob makes Judah a promise about something a king holds. It will not depart from Judah until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his.

cards.question: Jacob promises Judah that the ___ will not depart from him.

cards.text: Then Jacob says Judah ties his donkey to the vine and washes his garments in wine. Friend, my apron gets washed in plain old water, and this man is doing laundry in WINE.

cards.question: Jacob's picture of Judah keeps going: eyes darker than wine and teeth whiter than milk. What kind of life does it all show?

cards.text: Zebulun gets an OCEAN view: he'll live by the seashore and become a harbor for ships, with his border reaching to Sidon. Then Issachar, a strong donkey, lying down between the sheepfolds.

cards.question: Issachar sees that his resting place is good and his land is pleasant. What does he do?

answers.text: He bends his shoulder to the burden
He packs up and heads for Egypt
He fights his brothers for more land

cards.text: Dan will provide justice for his people as one of the tribes of Israel. Then Jacob says Dan will be a snake by the road, a viper in the path that bites the horse's heels.

cards.question: Dan the snake bites the horse's heels, and its rider tumbles ___.
Right in the middle of blessing his sons, Jacob stops and speaks one short line to someone else. Who does he speak to?
Jacob says Gad will be attacked by raiders and will never fight back.

cards.text: Asher's food will be rich, and he'll provide royal delicacies. Friend, I bake cookies for a LIVING, and I'm still a little jealous.
Naphtali is a doe set free that bears beautiful fawns. Then comes Joseph, a fruitful vine by a spring, whose branches scale the wall.
But it hasn't been easy for Joseph. The archers attacked him with bitterness and aimed at him in hostility.

cards.question: The archers aim at Joseph in hostility. What does Joseph do?

answers.text: He drops his bow and runs

cards.question: Jacob says Joseph's strong arms were tempered by someone's hands. Whose?

cards.text: The Almighty blesses Joseph with blessings of the heavens above and blessings of the depths below, and friend, that's not a sprinkle of blessing, that's the WHOLE JAR.

cards.question: Jacob wants his blessings to rest on Joseph's head. He calls Joseph the prince of his brothers.
Last comes Benjamin. Jacob calls him a ravenous ___ that devours the prey in the morning and divides the plunder in the evening.
When Jacob is done, he has given all twelve sons the exact same blessing.

cards.text: Then Jacob gives his sons one last instruction. He's about to be gathered to his people, and he tells them where to bury him.

cards.question: Jacob wants to be buried with his ___ in a cave in the land of ___.

cards.text: It's the cave in the field Abraham bought as a burial site, where Abraham and Sarah are buried, and Isaac and Rebekah. And Jacob buried one of his own wives there too.

cards.question: Which of his wives did Jacob bury in the cave with Abraham and Isaac?

cards.text: When Jacob finishes instructing his sons, he pulls his feet into the bed, breathes his last, and is gathered to his people. But stay close, friend, because this family's story isn't finished yet.

findings.problem: The joke builds a scenario around the baker's own parent ("when your father says 'Gather around,' you put the cookie DOWN"). That is a parent scenario, not a comparison from adult life.

rule.text: No jokes or scenarios about school, parents or anything aimed at kids. Work, bosses and bills are fine.

findings.problem: "But hold on to your apron, friend" tells the baker a reversal is coming. That gives away the answer to the true/false on card 4, which asks whether Reuben will keep on excelling.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke is a dad scenario with a school image ("when Dad lumps you in with your brother, it is NEVER for a gold star").

rule.text: No jokes or scenarios about school, parents or anything aimed at kids. Work, bosses and bills are fine.

findings.problem: Card 9 tells the baker that Jacob curses their anger. After a curse, the wrong answers "crown" and "honor" are ruled out, so only "scatter" fits.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 11 says the first three sons had it rough, and the question says Judah's turn "sounds very different." Together they rule out both negative wrong answers ("Turn on him and drive him out" and "Forget him and leave him behind").

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 13 quotes "like a lioness, who dares to rouse him?" right before the baker is asked whether the lion picture makes Judah sound weak and easy to push around. The setup line answers the question outright.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card calls Genesis 49:10 a promise ("Jacob makes Judah a promise"), and card 16 repeats it ("Jacob promises Judah"). The text frames these words as what will happen (49:1) and as blessings (49:28). It never calls them a promise.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Card 15 says the missing word is "something a king holds." That rules out the wrong answers "altar" and "tent," because neither is something a king holds.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the next word of Jacob's line ("its rider tumbles ___": backward, forward or sideways). Nothing the baker has seen lets them reason it out, so this tests wording, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The right answer "The LORD" is two words. The wrong answers, "Pharaoh king of Egypt" and "Laban his uncle," are three and four words. The short right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question is Jacob's line with one word blanked ("a ravenous ___ that devours the prey"). No earlier card gives context for Benjamin's picture, so the baker can only guess the wording.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
